description: Which engine consumes which vector family. npm run validate (tools/validate/vector-coverage.mjs) reads every family under spec/test-vectors, searches each engine's test roots for a consumer, and fails when a family has neither a consumer nor an exclusion below. A consumer is a test source that names the family as `<family>.json` or `vector("<family>")`. Adding a vector therefore means adding it to every engine, or writing down here why an engine is exempt. Adding an engine means adding an entry here with its test roots; an engine whose roots do not exist yet is reported as absent and skipped, so the entry can be written before the code.
families_note: A family is one spec/test-vectors/<family>.json file, or the http-golden/ directory as the single family `http-golden`.

exclusions.provider-route.crypto-usdt: Provider wizard route data; the wizard is browser-side (@openreceive/provider-data) and the Ruby engine ships no wizard.

exclusions.fiat-to-msats.usd: BTCPay owns fiat rates (plugin plan 0.13); the plugin ports no price math.
exclusions.rate-limit-window: BTCPay owns request budgets and store permissions; the plugin mounts no OpenReceive HTTP routes.
exclusions.http-golden: The plugin exposes BTCPay-shaped routes, not the OpenReceive HTTP contract (plugin plan 0.17).
exclusions.provider-route.crypto-usdt: Provider wizard route data; the plugin ships no wizard (plugin plan 0.11).
